source: static-fallback (committed; last rung of the CONTRACTS.md 2.2 price ladder)
note: Used only when neither $HARNESS_PRICE_SNAPSHOT nor ./lambdactl types can answer. A run priced from this file is marked flags.provenance_incomplete — resolve_price() calls res.provenance(), and CONTRACTS.md 2.2 rung (3) says the same: the price is approximate, the verdicts are not affected, and aggregate.py still counts the run. (This line used to say flags.nonconformant, which is the opposite consequence: aggregate.py drops nonconformant runs from the headline numbers.) Refresh from ./lambdactl types and re-commit whenever Lambda list prices change.
refresh_note: 2026-09-09: refreshed from the live /instance-types payload. The 2026-08-30 table had drifted about a third low across the board — gpu_1x_h100_pcie 249 -> 329 (+32%), gpu_8x_h100_sxm5 2392 -> 3192 (+33%) — so every cost_usd computed off this rung understated the real bill by that much. The table now carries every published instance type, not just the four this benchmark dispatches to: resolve_price() gives up entirely on a missing key (price unresolved, cost cannot be computed), and the extra rows cost nothing. regions_with_capacity stays [] for every entry on purpose — Lambda capacity turns over within the hour, so a committed region list is stale before the next run; [] honestly says 'this file does not know'. Capacity is context that only the live rungs of the ladder can supply.
